# chengyu: # line order = order in which idiom cards are introduced

origin / note: A folk story tells of a painter whose half-tiger, half-horse picture confused his sons; the phrase became a byword for carelessness. In daily speech it just means "so-so".
A set phrase rather than a classical idiom. English "long time no see" is often said to be a word-for-word copy of it.
Said when seeing someone off.

meaning: bon voyage; may your trip go smoothly
origin / note: A tailwind the whole way. Some people jokingly avoid it for flights, because planes take off into the wind.

meaning: may everything go as you wish
origin / note: A favorite New Year and birthday greeting.
Greeting-card classic: what the heart thinks of, comes true.
The Chinese New Year greeting. Kids like to reply 红包拿来: "hand over the red envelope!"
Mountains and seas of people: think of any big station during a holiday.
As if cast from the same mold. Here 模 is read mú, not mó.
The numbers seven and eight often mean "all over the place" in idioms.
From the saying about fifteen buckets in a well: seven going up, eight going down. Your heart can't settle.
Five colors, six colors: more colors than you can count.
Self speaks, self talks.
Looking east, gazing west: eyes everywhere.
Half believing, half doubting.

meaning: largely the same, with minor differences
origin / note: The big things are the same, the small things differ.
One look, and all feelings are focused on one person.
Originally a Buddhist term for truths beyond thought and words.
Nobody can name its secret.

meaning: to kill two birds with one stone
origin / note: One action, two gains.

meaning: to kill two birds with one stone
origin / note: A modern loan from the European saying; 一举两得 is the native equivalent.

meaning: when in Rome, do as the Romans do
origin / note: When you enter a village, follow its customs.
One look and everything is clear.
A thousand methods, a hundred plans.
Carts flowing like water, horses like a long dragon.
The moment the war horse arrives, the battle is won. A common wish before exams.
The historian Sima Qian wrote that his death would matter as little as one hair from nine oxen.
A sail with a favorable wind all the way. Also a wish.
An old oil seller could pour oil through the hole of a coin without wetting it. "Nothing special," he said, "just practice."
LLM tie-in (optional): That's training: enough gradient steps and the skill emerges.

meaning: review the old to learn the new
origin / note: From Confucius' Analects: whoever reviews the old and gains new insight can be a teacher.
LLM tie-in (optional): Spaced repetition in four characters: what FSRS schedules for you every day.

origin / note: Follow the proper order and advance gradually.
LLM tie-in (optional): Curriculum learning: train on easy examples first, harder ones later.

meaning: the slow need to start early
origin / note: A clumsy bird takes off first. Often said modestly about oneself.

meaning: constant effort wears down any obstacle
origin / note: Dripping water eventually bores through stone. Like your daily epoch.
Stopping in the middle of the road.
Confucius: if I show a student one corner and he can't work out the other three, I don't repeat the lesson.
LLM tie-in (optional): Generalization: from a few examples to unseen cases, like few-shot prompting.

origin / note: General Zhao Kuo knew every military text by heart, then lost a huge army at the battle of Changping.
Like a legendary horse that runs a thousand li in one day.

meaning: to keep improving what is already good
origin / note: Already fine, still seeking finer.
LLM tie-in (optional): Fine-tuning a model that is already good.

meaning: half the effort, twice the result
origin / note: The opposite is 事倍功半: twice the work, half the result.
LLM tie-in (optional): What quantization promises: most of the quality at a fraction of the memory.

origin / note: The painter Wen Tong pictured the whole bamboo in his mind before his brush touched the paper.
A painter left his dragons without eyes. When he dotted them in, the dragons came alive and flew away.

meaning: to hit the nail on the head
origin / note: One needle and blood shows: straight to the point. Here 血 is read xiě.

meaning: to wait for luck instead of working
origin / note: A farmer saw a rabbit run into a tree stump and die. He gave up farming to wait by the stump for more rabbits.

meaning: to ruin something by overdoing it
origin / note: In a race to draw a snake for a jug of wine, the fastest man added feet. "Snakes have no feet," said another, and took the wine.

meaning: to talk to the wrong audience
origin / note: A musician played beautiful music to an ox, which kept chewing grass.

meaning: someone with a narrow view of the world
origin / note: A frog at the bottom of a well thinks the sky is as big as the well's opening.
After a wolf took a sheep, the shepherd finally mended the pen, and lost no more.
A man sold a spear that pierces any shield and a shield no spear can pierce. "And if your spear hits your shield?" That's why 矛盾 means contradiction.

meaning: to bully others with someone else's power
origin / note: A fox walked ahead of a tiger. The animals fled from the tiger, and the fox claimed they feared him.
A man dropped his sword from a moving boat, carved a mark on the side, and later searched the water below the mark.
A thief covered his own ears while stealing a bell, sure that if he couldn't hear it, nobody could.
A farmer pulled his rice seedlings up a little to help them grow faster. The next day they had all withered.
LLM tie-in (optional): A learning rate that's too high: the loss explodes instead of going down.

origin / note: An old man lost his horse; it came back with another. His son broke a leg riding it, which kept him out of a deadly war.

meaning: to be scared of imaginary dangers
origin / note: A guest saw a snake in his wine and fell ill. It was only the reflection of a bow hanging on the wall.
A keeper offered his monkeys three nuts in the morning and four at night. They protested, so he offered four and three, and they were delighted.
Cao Cao told his thirsty soldiers there was a plum grove ahead. Their mouths watered, and they marched on.

meaning: to burn one's bridges; all in
origin / note: General Xiang Yu sank his boats and smashed the cooking pots, so his army could only win or die.
The minister Zhao Gao presented a deer to the emperor as a horse, to see which officials dared contradict him.

meaning: to judge the whole from one part
origin / note: Blind men each touched one part of an elephant and argued: it's a wall, a rope, a pillar, a fan…
LLM tie-in (optional): Each attention head sees one pattern; only together do they see the elephant.

origin / note: A parrot imitating human speech.
LLM tie-in (optional): The "stochastic parrot" critique of LLMs, two thousand years early.

meaning: errors spread and grow as they are passed on
origin / note: Each retelling adds to the mistake.
LLM tie-in (optional): Like models trained on their own hallucinations: errors compound.

meaning: to work in isolation, ignoring reality
origin / note: Building a cart behind closed doors, never checking it fits the road.
LLM tie-in (optional): Training without evaluation on real data.

meaning: actions that work against one's goal
origin / note: A man heading to the southern state of Chu drove north, boasting of his fast horses and plentiful money.
Drawing a pancake to fill an empty stomach.

meaning: to amaze everyone with a sudden success
origin / note: A king compared himself to a bird that hadn't sung for three years: "When it sings, it will astonish everyone."
Besieged Xiang Yu heard songs of his homeland Chu from every side and thought his own people had defected.

meaning: professed love that vanishes when faced with the real thing
origin / note: Lord Ye filled his house with dragon carvings. When a real dragon came to visit, he fled in terror.

meaning: to endure hardship to prepare a comeback
origin / note: After his defeat, King Goujian slept on brushwood and tasted bitter gall every day so he would never forget.
